item.title: UN Security Council holds emergency session on ceasefire
item.body: The UN Security Council met overnight to discuss a ceasefire resolution. Diplomats said talks continued and a vote was expected within days. The border remains closed and aid convoys are waiting.

item.title: Markets rally as central bank holds interest rates
item.body: Stock markets rose on Tuesday after the central bank kept interest rates unchanged. Investors welcomed the decision, citing stable inflation and strong GDP growth. Oil prices also edged higher.

item.title: Startup unveils AI chip for data centers
item.body: A startup announced a new AI chip designed for data centers, promising faster software training. Analysts said the chip could increase competition in the semiconductor market and push down prices.

item.title: Le Parlement adopte la loi sur le climat
item.body: Le Parlement a adopté une nouvelle loi sur le climat visant à réduire les émissions. Le gouvernement a salué ce vote, tandis que l'opposition a critiqué le calendrier. Les sénateurs ont aussi voté un amendement.

item.title: WHO reports progress in new vaccine rollout
item.body: The World Health Organization said the new vaccine rollout is progressing well. Hospitals reported fewer cases and doctors praised the campaign. A new study in a medical journal supports the results.

item.title: Underdogs win the championship final
item.body: The underdog team won the football championship final on Sunday. The coach said the players deserved the trophy after a tense match. Fans celebrated in the streets and the league announced a parade.

item.title: ارتفاع مؤشرات البورصة بعد قرار البنك المركزي
item.body: ارتفعت مؤشرات البورصة بعد قرار البنك المركزي بإبقاء أسعار الفائدة دون تغيير. رحّب المستثمرون بالقرار مشيرين إلى استقرار التضخم.

item.title: Study links ocean warming to stronger storms
item.body: A new study published in a scientific journal links rising ocean temperatures to stronger storms. Researchers said NASA satellite data supports the findings and called for more research on climate.
